theorem_title: The target–sensor determinant is n plus one
natural_language_statement:
On $\mathbb Z^2$, set $q=(1,0)$ and $r_n=(1,n+1)$ for $n\in\mathbb N$, and write $\det(a,b)=a_1b_2-a_2b_1$.

$$
\det(q,r_n)=n+1.
$$

This exact integer identity supplies the target–sensor minors in the rank-two example. Natural indices include n=0.
formal_statement:
theorem NewMathDiscovery.LinearBlindness.RankTwoInstability.target_sensor_minor (n : Nat) :
    determinant targetRow (sensorRow n) = Int.ofNat n + 1 := by sorry
